title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The ordering convention (k<i meaning X_k lies in the closure of X_i) is used consistently, but the page never says whether the index set is totally ordered or only a poset. 'i<k<j' implicitly needs a total order or chain condition.
In Σ_{(i,j)}, Tub° must mean the boundary sphere bundle ∂Tub, not the open tube T̊ub. The notation is ambiguous, and the definition only makes sense with the boundary reading.

In the V_{ij} formula the intersection is taken with V(X*_i, X_j) itself. Whether V(X*_i, X_j) is meant inside X_j or inside the closure of X_j is not specified, so the removal of intermediate strata is only heuristic here.
The commutative diagram for V_{ijk} is incomplete: there are struck-out terms, and the bottom-row target is unclear.

ideas.what: Cutting a stratified space with control data into manifolds with corners Σ_{i_0…i_n} indexed by chains of strata, by removing open tubular neighbourhoods; the resulting contravariant diagram over flags reconstructs X.
ideas.modern_name: Unfolding / resolution of a Thom–Mather (or conically smooth) stratified space into manifolds with (fibred) corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather/Thom control data (1970s); Verona (1984); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip' (2017); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza resolution (2012)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 (dévissage of tame stratified structures, announced in outline only)

ideas.what: Boundary-of-tube pieces Σ_{(i,j)} ↪ Σ_j fibering over Σ_i, i.e. link bundles, with intermediate tubes removed.
ideas.modern_name: Link bundles / boundary faces of the resolved space (fibred-corner structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather; Melrose school (manifolds with fibred corners)

ideas.what: Diagram of neighbourhood-deleted spaces V_{ij} → X*_i, with V_{ijk} mapping to V_{ij} and V_{jk}: a system of links with composition-like structure for chains i<j<k.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / exit-path category of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988, homotopy links); MacPherson; Treumann (2009); Woolf; Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A)

missed.claim: Alongside the geometric unfolding, Grothendieck sets up a second system V_{ij}, V_{ijk} of deleted neighbourhoods fibred over strata, with maps for each chain i<j<k. This is the combinatorics of homotopy links and exit paths (functors on the chain category of the poset), written about 1981–82, before Quinn's homotopy links (1988) and the exit-path ∞-category. It points to an early, unpublished homotopical form of the dévissage conjecture of the Esquisse.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck as an early originator of the idea that a stratified space is modelled by a diagram over the chains of its stratifying poset. This matters historically for the stratified homotopy hypothesis (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine, Douteau–Waas).

deep.surprise_reason: The geometric unfolding is announced in the Esquisse and is now standard (Verona, ALMP, AFT). The parallel homotopy-link diagram is an interesting early anticipation of exit-path ideas. However, it is fragmentary here, and the overall programme is already attributed to Grothendieck in outline.
transcription_corrections: The phrase after Σ_{i_0 i_1…i_n} reads approximately '[struck word] foncteur contravariant par rapport aux diagrammes variables (i_0,…,i_n)', not 'fonctions correspondant aux diagrammes'.
Under the union in Σ_{(i,j)}: the struck condition is 'k<j'; the retained conditions are 'k≠i' and 'i<k<j'.
In Σ_i the union is ⋃_{k<i} T̊ub(X_k, X_i), with an open-tube circle over T.
The margin '[?] dim' at upper left looks like an arrow labelled with a small symbol, possibly 'd'. The rotated bottom-left text reads roughly 'λ_i T = λ'_i T … = Σ(…)', which is illegible.
